To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the T cell repertoire in the Mtv- mice was reproducible and was not affected by background genes, 2) vSAGs deleted T cells with the predicted specificity, 3) vSAG11, which was previously shown to have a very low avidity for V beta 8, positively selects T cells bearing Vbeta 8.2, 4) the effects of vSAgs were similar in thymocytes, peripheral CD4 T cells and peripheral
vSAG3, - 8, and - 9, and possibly vSAG11, are expressed in thymus, spleen, and lymph nodes and delete V beta 4, 5, 6, 7, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 17 T cells, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Mtv's in the development of T cells and their effect on the TCR repertoire.
the effect of vSAG's on the T cell receptor repertoire of mice with single endogenous Mtv.
the effects of endogenously expressed superantigens upon the T cell repertoire in the absence of foreign superantigens and with the effects of foreign superantigen on the T cell receptor repertoire.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vSAGs are not the primary driving forces in the selection of the T cell repertoire.
the T cell repertoire is affected by endogenous Mtv vSAGs in a complex manner.
endogenous viral super-antigins have no major effect upon the T cell repertoire in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T cell repertoire in Mtv-negative mice is very similar to the repertoire in Mtv- positive mice.

the effects of Mtv superantigen on the T cell receptor V beta repertoire are limited, and that most of the effects on the T cell repertories of Mtv-positive and Mtv-negative mice can be explained by positive and negative selection in the thymus by class I and classII major histocompatibility complexes.
the T cell repertoire in mice is affected by the major histocompatibility complexes and endogenous viral super antigens, but not by any other endogenous superantiger.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T cell repertoire in mice with multiple Mtv's can be predicted from the repertoire in Mtv-negative mice, with the addition of the effects of each vSAG.
the T cell repetoire in mice can be studied without the confounding effects of endogenous vSAGs, and that the effects of v SAGs on the T cell receptor repertoire can be studied in single-Mtv lines.
vSAGs are not as potent as foreign SAGs and that they have only a limited effect upon T cell development and the T cell repertoire.
